claim: On-demand communication (ODC) improves device utilization and training throughput in LLM post-training tasks compared to fully sharded data parallelism (FSDP), achieving up to 36% speedup.
falsifier: Reproduce the comparison on a different LLM post-training workload with imbalanced sequence lengths; measure throughput and device utilization for ODC vs. FSDP.

conditions: LLM post-training tasks including supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL)
Workloads with high variance in sequence lengths causing imbalance
exclusions: Limited to the reported experimental setup: specific model sizes, hardware, and post-training tasks; transfer to other settings is unestablished.

title: Replacing collective all-gather for Device utilization and end-to-end

claim: The magnitude of post-training-induced geopolitical bias in large language models is modulated by the language used to prompt the model, with prompting in the developer's language amplifying the bias.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by evaluating post-trained LLMs from different developers using forced-choice probes in multiple languages, including the developer's native language, and comparing bias magnitudes.

conditions: evaluated using paired-scenario forced-choice probes over 28 country pairs
tested on post-trained variants of open-weight LLMs
observed for Mistral (pro-France under French prompting) and descriptively for five of seven models under Chinese prompting
exclusions: limited to the seven open-weight LLM families tested
limited to English, French, and Chinese prompt languages
limited to the forced-choice probe methodology
transferability to other languages or models is unestablished

title: Prompt language–magnitude of geopolitical bias mechanism
